newsitem.title: UK: Greycoat responds to rebel shareholder move.
newsitem.headline: Greycoat responds to rebel shareholder move.

text.p: UK property company Greycoat Plc said on Thursday it was pleased that rebel shareholder UK Active Value Fund (UKAV) had decided to abstain from voting at a special meeting it called to propose the break-up of the group.

"We regret the unnecessary diversion and cost over the last two months but we are pleased to note that UKAV has now recognised the shortcomings of its proposal," Greycoat chairman Michael Beckett said in a statement.
The reconvened extraordinary general meeting is due to take place at 1200 GMT.

UKAV said on Wednesday it had realised its immediate goals following discussions with Greycoat's chief executive and anticipated "further progress towards unlocking shareholder value". This, it said, followed Greycoat's confirmation that it would sell its Embankment Place development in central London.

Greycoat said in response that UKAV's estimate -- that this disposal should result in some 100 million stg of equity being returned to shareholders -- was "a gross overstatement of the equity the company has invested in this property".
It also denied it had seen detailed merger proposals from its smaller rival, Moorfield Estates.
Active Value Advisers, which advises UKAV, said it believed Moorfield's proposals "have considerable merit and could better serve the interests of the Greycoat shareholders".

UKAV said it would continue to monitor the progress of Moorfield's proposals and Greycoat's realisation of its main properties but reserved the right to call an EGM "if further attempts to unlock value for shareholders are frustrated".
Greycoat's Beckett said in his statement that the company had "a well-defined strategy" and was "committed to delivering value for all shareholders".
